engineNeeds.need: digits driver with shared digit and segment pins (MAX6950/MAX6951)
engineNeeds.keys: display (driver digits): "sharedPins": 9 pin names; "segmentLines": ["dp","g","f","e","d","c","b","a"] (the segment each of the 8 non-selected pins carries, in pin order; each of a b c d e f g dp once); replaces digitPins/segmentPins. Digit k < digits is selected on sharedPins[k] (digitActive level); the other eight pins carry digit k's segments: lit = segmentActive level, unlit = released (Z); shutdown releases every pin; test lights every segment in every slot; segmentBits (8 entries, order a b c d e f g dp), decode, decodeField, ram, scan, blank as before.
engineNeeds.why: max6950-max6951 p.5-6 Table 1: pin DIG/SEGk is both digit k's cathode and a segment line of the other digits; unlit segments are high impedance (p.5, Figure 4 p.13). The digits driver names a pin once (pin "X" is used twice), and a lit-low/unlit-high segment level would light ghost segments through the shared cathodes.
engineNeeds.status: implemented and tested in scratchpad/g2/max695x-display.patch (max6950_test: 8 LSHD-7503 displays wired as Table 1)

engineNeeds.keys: display.scanLimit: a field name; only digits 0 to its value are scanned (field >= digits-1: all); the other digits' pins are never selected. A display test scans every digit.
engineNeeds.why: max6950-max6951 p.9, Table 12 p.11: scan-limit register 0x03 (power-up 4: five digits); p.8 display test scans eight digits
engineNeeds.status: implemented and tested in the patch

engineNeeds.need: second RAM plane shown in the second half of a blink period
engineNeeds.keys: display.blink: {"enable": condition, "ram": [one field per digit], "halfPeriodUs": n or {"field": "REG.F", "values": {...}}}: while enable holds, digit k shows its ram field (display.ram) when floor(now / half) is even and the blink.ram field when it is odd (decode applies to the shown value); the period counts from simulated time 0.
engineNeeds.why: max6950-max6951 p.10-11, Tables 7, 8, 17, 18 (p.16): planes P0 and P1 alternate, 1 s each (B = 0) or 0.5 s (B = 1) at 4 MHz
engineNeeds.status: implemented and tested in the patch

engineNeeds.need: (optional) restart of the blink and multiplex counters
engineNeeds.keys: a command or a field write that sets the blink phase origin and the scan slot to now / 0 (CONFIG.T = 1 on CS rising)
engineNeeds.why: max6950-max6951 p.7, p.10 Table 9: the T bit clears the OSC divider chain and resets the multiplex sequence; not modeled (phase counts from time 0)

engineNeeds.need: ports driver: open-drain LED sink mode, weak pullup mode, read-back field, shutdown and test
engineNeeds.keys: display.ports[i]: "sinkValues": dirField values for which the pin drives 0 while dataField is nonzero and is released otherwise; "pullupValues": dirField values for which the pin is an input with a weak 1; "readField": a field refreshed on every register or pin change with dataField (output and sink) or the pin level, Z reading 0 (input); display.shutdown: every port released (no pullup) except sink ports while display.test holds; display.test: every sink port drives 0. push-pull outputs are untouched by test.
engineNeeds.why: max6957 p.6 Table 2 (00 LED sink where the register bit 1 means pin low, 01 push-pull, 10 input, 11 input with pullup), p.7 shutdown forces inputs, p.13 display test turns on LED ports only and p.7 overrides shutdown. The existing ports driver has one polarity and one direction per port, no weak pullup and no read-back (a port register bit reads the pin for an input). `pins.levels` would copy the pin into the data field and overwrite an output's data.
engineNeeds.status: implemented and tested in the patch (max6957_test)

engineNeeds.need: MAX6957 transition detection and the INT output on P31
engineNeeds.keys: e.g. display.ports.transition: {"enable": "CONFIG.M=1", "pins": [P24 .. P30], "mask": "MASK.M", "output": "P31", "snapshotOn": "CONFIG", "clearOn": "MASK"}. Semantics (max6957 p.10, Figure 6 p.14): a bus write of CONFIG with M = 1 takes a 7-bit snapshot of the watched pin levels, clears the INT latch and arms detection; while armed, a change of any watched pin whose mask bit is 1 from its snapshot, even a short pulse, sets the INT latch for good; while M = 1 and P31 is a GPIO output (PC28.P31 = 01) P31 drives the INT latch instead of its data bit; any bus read or write of MASK clears the latch and disarms detection (one shot, until CONFIG is written with M = 1 again).
engineNeeds.why: max6957 p.10: seven maskable ports P24-P30 flag changes on P31. The converter engine has no hook on a bus access to a register and no pin-change event for the display driver beyond a refresh; registers CONFIG.M and MASK exist and are stored, P31 is an ordinary port.

engineNeeds.keys: bus.misoIdle: "drive" (the shift register's last bit while CS is high)
engineNeeds.why: max6957 p.7: "DOUT on the MAX6957 is never high impedance"; the engine's MISO is Z while CS is high.
engineNeeds.status: not implemented, no effect on a single-chip bus

notes: Four devices: MAX6950 (5 digits) and MAX6951 (8 digits) from max6950-max6951, MAX6957 (28 ports: AAX 36-pin SSOP, ATL 40-pin TQFN) and MAX6957-20 (20 ports: AAI 28-pin SSOP, ANI 28-pin DIP) from max6957; 8 + 7 parts: MAX6950/MAX6951 x {CEE, EEE} x {+, +T}, MAX6957AAX+/+T, ATL+/+T, AAI+/+T, ANI+ (Analog Devices; the stock check is the main thread's: plan-56-D notes say EEE+ is last time buy). The devices only LOAD with scratchpad/g2/max695x-display.patch applied (git apply from the repo root; it touches backend/src/models/display_out.c, display_out.h, converter_load.c, backend/tests/display_out_test.c (rejects, and the unknown-key test now uses 'sparkle' because 'blink' is a key now) and docs/parts-format.md); without it neither MAX6950/51 (sharedPins) nor MAX6957 (sinkValues, pullupValues, readField) load. Benches: max6950_test.c and max6957_test.c (add logic_test(max6950_test) and logic_test(max6957_test) to backend/CMakeLists.txt after display_out_test). In the scratch build: max6950_test, max6957_test and display_out_test pass; library_check passes; listing_check, trace_check and footprint_check fail only with 'extra part / extra footprint (not in the golden)' lines (15 parts, and the footprints), so regenerate parts.txt, traces.txt, footprints.txt (additions only). Footprints: QSOP-16-EP is drawn from p.19; SSOP-28 and PDIP-28-600 exist and were matched by package (A28-1 28 SSOP, N28-2 28 PDIP) because the sheet has no drawings (documents 21-0056, 21-0043 not in hand, verify); SSOP-36-A36-4 and TQFN-40-6X6-T4066 are missing (names used by the parts; the benches ran with TEMPORARY placeholder footprints of those names, which are not delivered: draw them before merging, or the AAX and ATL parts do not load). Datasheet URLs follow the Analog Devices pattern and were not verified (analog.com timed out): max6950-max6951.pdf, MAX6957.pdf. MAX6957 modeling: the read-back goes through the next frame (command byte then data) as p.10 says, port bits read the pin for inputs, port registers P4-P11 of the 20-port parts store but read 0, transition detection/INT not modeled, config I and current registers stored only. MAX6950/51: write-only, blink with planes, scan limit, hex decode per digit, R clear, test overrides shutdown, hi-Z when shut. Known limits that were avoided: no [REG] in an `in` pattern (capture letters and set), one decode per device (hex only).
